Subject: Question on invoice #BR-2025-05 (mid-cycle cutoff / proration)

Hi Jordan,

We were reviewing invoice BR-2025-05 and noticed a couple oddities around the mid-cycle cutoff on May 3. Our engineering team ran a bulk reingest on May 2 at 23:50 PDT which produced a short-lived spike; we expected that to be pro-rated into the June bill rather than counted fully in the May invoice. The line item shows a 37% token overage relative to our forecast.

Can you confirm:
- Which cutoff window Redwood used for our account (UTC vs. local)?
- Whether there was an automatic proration applied for mid-cycle bursts?
- If not prorated, can you provide raw meter samples around 2025-05-02T23:30:00 to 2025-05-03T00:30:00? We'll need the CSV for our audit.

Also, we are EU-registered (BrightCart US entity billed to BrightCart EU), so if there's a retro credit please include VAT classification for our tax team.

I've attached the invoice and a short usage summary from our side. Thanks — we need a response by EOD Monday if possible so we can close our internal month.

Best,
Andi Lopez
Senior Finance Operations
BrightCart

Subject: Re: Question on invoice #BR-2025-05 (mid-cycle cutoff / proration)

Hi Andi — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments. Looping in Ben (billing ops) and Grace (your account lead) to get the technical trace and policy confirmation.

Quick answers up front:
- Our standard cutoff is UTC 00:00 for most accounts; for BrightCart you're on the default window (UTC).
- We do not automatically move a burst into the next cycle unless it is explicitly marked as a "delayed ingest" via the Ingest Tagging API or if a replay window flag was set by your infra team prior to the spike.

Ben — can you pull the meter samples for 2025-05-02T23:15:00Z through 2025-05-03T00:45:00Z and confirm whether the requests were attributed to a staging key or to the production API key? If it's a staging key we typically apply a manual proration/credit. Please also flag whether any downstream tokenization normalization happened (we've seen some clients hit duplicate tokenization counting when chunking changes happened during reingest).

Andi — we'll aim to get the CSV and an initial recommendation by EOD Monday. If we need to propose a credit, we'll include VAT notes for your EU tax team.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Internal note (billing ops findings so far) — not sent to customer.

Hi team,

I pulled the ingestion and request logs for BR-4391 across the requested window (converted to UTC): 2025-05-03T06:15:00Z through 2025-05-03T07:45:00Z (system stored UTC). Key observations:
- We see a ~14M token spike between 06:38:00Z and 06:52:00Z originating from API key prod-ck-42 (production key) — confirmed request IDs present in the main ledger.
- There is a separate cluster at 06:50:00Z that shows requests attributed to sandbox-ck-09 (staging). That cluster is small (~120k tokens) but overlaps the production window.
- Tokenization analysis: the client changed chunk_size from 512->1024 in their reingest; we have evidence this caused tokenization normalization differences resulting in higher per-call token counts by ~8% for identical text.

Preliminary recommendation:
1) Production-origin requests from prod-ck-42 are billable on May invoice (cutoff is UTC 00:00).
2) The sandbox-ck-09 cluster should be considered for manual proration — it's <1% of the spike but the timing overlaps.
3) For the tokenization normalization effect, propose a one-time goodwill credit equal to the estimated delta (8% of sessions inside the spike window) and propose labeling that credit as VAT-exempt adjustment if BrightCart provides a signed attestation that the changes were part of a test/reingest job.

I attached the raw meter samples for the window and a short CSV summarizing per-request attribution. If we proceed with a credit, finance needs an authorization (Jordan or Grace) and a HubSpot doc link to attach the evidence.

Ben Carter
Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: inference_window_logs_202505.csv
From: Andi Lopez <andi.lopez@brightcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: billing+recon@brightcart.com
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 10:41:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on invoice #BR-2025-05 (mid-cycle cutoff / proration)

Thanks Jordan & Ben — this is helpful.

We confirm that the 23:50 PDT reingest was initiated by our production infra (prod-ck-42) as part of a backfill run — it was not meant to be a staging job. Our infra team changed chunk_size mid-run because older parts of the dataset were encoded with a different chunking heuristic.

Given that, we accept the production attribution. For the tokenization normalization delta, BrightCart requests a goodwill credit for the estimated 8% delta on the spike window and a note we can pass to our tax team indicating the credit will be treated as a billing adjustment (non-taxable rebate) in the US; if Redwood can provide the same language for EU VAT treatment that would help our EU accounting.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
- A short support doc stating the credit amount calculation and that it is a billing adjustment (to attach to our month-end).
- Confirmation of the final credit amount and whether Redwood will classify it as VAT-exempt or provide supporting documentation for our EU filing.

Appreciate the quick triage — please flag if you need a signed attestation from our infra team.

Regards,
Andi Lopez
BrightCart — Finance Ops
